question:
A technician needs to provide remote support for a legacy Linux-based operating system from their Windows laptop. The solution needs to allow
 the technician to see what the user is doing and provide the ability to interact with the user's session. Which of the following remote access
 technologies would support the use case?
explanation: B (VNC) is platform independent and shares the actual console session, so the technician on Windows can watch what the Linux user is doing and take control of the same screen. D (RDP) is Windows-oriented and normally opens a separate session rather than mirroring the user's. C (SSH) provides only a command-line shell, giving no view of the graphical session. A (VPN) simply tunnels network traffic and offers no remote control at all.

question:
A technician is attempting to join a workstation to a domain but is receiving an error message stating the domain cannot be found. However, the
technician is able to ping the server and access the internet. Given the following information:
Which of the following should the technician do to fix the issue?
explanation: A (Change the DNS settings) is right because joining a domain depends on resolving the domain's SRV records to find a domain controller, and a wrong DNS server (for example a public resolver instead of the internal DC) breaks that lookup while leaving everything else working. Successful pings and internet access already prove the IP configuration and routing are sound, which rules out D (Default gateway) and C (Subnet mask). B (Static IP) addresses nothing here since connectivity is fine.

question:
A network technician notices that most of the company's network switches are now end-of-life and need to be upgraded. Which of the following
 should the technician do first?
explanation: C (Propose the change) comes first: the technician documents the scope, risk, rollback plan and business justification in a change request. Only then can the change advisory board weigh in. B (Approve the change) is the board's job and cannot happen without a submitted proposal, D (Schedule the change) follows approval so a maintenance window can be agreed, and A (Implement the change) is last. Acting out of order bypasses the risk assessment entirely.

question:
MFA for a custom web application on a user's smartphone is no longer working. The last time the user remembered it working was before taking a
 vacation to another country. Which of the following should the technician do first?

options.A: Verify the date and time settings.

explanation: A (Verify the date and time settings) is first because time-based one-time passwords are generated from a shared secret plus the current clock, so a phone whose time zone or clock shifted during international travel produces codes the server rejects. The timing of the failure points straight at this. C (Uninstall and reinstall) risks losing the enrolled token seed for no reason, B (Apply mobile OS patches) is unrelated to clock skew, and D (Escalate to the developer) skips the obvious local check.

question: Which of the following is found in an MSDS sheet for a battery backup?
explanation: B (Emergency procedures) belongs on a safety data sheet, which documents hazards, safe handling and storage, first aid, spill and leak cleanup, firefighting measures and disposal for the battery's chemicals. That is the sheet's whole purpose. A (Installation instructions) and C (Configuration steps) come from the product manual, and D (Voltage specifications) is on the spec sheet or the unit's label, not the SDS.

question:
The screen of a previously working computer repeatedly displays an OS Not Found error message when the computer is started. Only a USB drive,
 a keyboard, and a mouse are plugged into the computer. Which of the following should a technician do first?

options.A: Run data recovery tools on the disk.
options.B: Partition the disk using the GPT format.

explanation: C (Check boot options) is the first and least invasive step, because a USB drive is plugged in and the firmware boot order has almost certainly put it ahead of the internal disk, so the system finds no operating system on it. B (Partition the disk using the GPT format) would wipe the user's data before the cause is even known. D (Switching from UEFI to BIOS) breaks a UEFI/GPT installation outright, and A (Data recovery tools) assumes a failed disk with no evidence yet.

question:
A security administrator teaches all of an organization's staff members to use BitLocker To Go. Which of the following best describes the reason
 for this training?

options.A: To ensure that all removable media is password protected in case of loss or theft
options.B: To enable Secure Boot and a BIOS-level password to prevent configuration changes
options.C: To enforce VPN connectivity to be encrypted by hardware modules
options.D: To configure all laptops to use the TPM as an encryption factor for hard drives

explanation: A is correct because BitLocker To Go is the removable-media arm of BitLocker: it encrypts USB flash drives and external disks and demands a password or smart card to unlock them, so a drive left in a taxi is unreadable. D (TPM-based drive encryption) describes standard BitLocker on internal disks, which needs no user training on removable media. B (Secure Boot and BIOS passwords) and C (VPN encryption) are entirely different controls.

question: Which of the following is used to detect and record access to restricted areas?
explanation: B (Video surveillance) both detects activity in a restricted area and keeps a recorded history of who entered and what they did, which is what the question asks for. C (Badge readers) authenticate and authorise entry and log the credential used, but they do not observe or record the area itself. A (Bollards) are vehicle barriers and D (Fence) is a perimeter deterrent, and neither detects or records anything. (Note: the dump prints C as the answer, but the highest-voted community discussion says B — we go with the community.)

question:
An administrator received an email stating that the OS they are currently supporting will no longer be issued security updates and patches. Which
 of the following is most likely the reason the administrator received this message?

options.A: Support from the computer’s manufacturer is expiring.
options.B: The OS will be considered end of life.
options.C: The built-in security software is being removed from the next OS version.
options.D: A new version of the OS will be released soon.

explanation: B (The OS will be considered end of life) is exactly what such a notice means: the vendor has set a date after which no security updates, patches or fixes will be issued, and organisations must migrate or accept the risk. A (Manufacturer support expiring) covers hardware warranty and drivers, which is a separate lifecycle. D (A new version being released) does not by itself stop patching for the current one, and C (Built-in security software being removed) is not what a patch cutoff notice announces.

question:
Which of the following is the best way to distribute custom images to 800 devices that include four device vendor classes with two types of user
 groups?

options.A: Use xcopy to clone the hard drives from one to another.
options.B: Use robocopy to move the files to each device.
options.C: Use a local image deployment tool for each device.
options.D: Use a network-based remote installation tool.

explanation: D (Use a network-based remote installation tool) is the only approach that scales, because a PXE or deployment-server solution can push different images to different hardware classes and user groups without a technician touching each of the 800 machines. A (xcopy) and B (robocopy) copy files but do not write partitions, boot records or a sysprepped system image. C (A local image deployment tool for each device) still requires visiting every workstation.

question: Which of the following types of social engineering attacks sends an unsolicited text message to a user's mobile device?
explanation: D (Smishing) is phishing delivered over SMS, where the attacker texts a link or a pretext to the victim's phone, exactly as described. B (Vishing) is the voice equivalent, carried out over a phone call rather than a message. C (Spear phishing) is a targeted email aimed at a specific individual using researched details, and A (Impersonation) is the broader tactic of posing as someone trusted rather than a delivery channel.

question:
A user reports some single sign-on errors to a help desk technician. Currently, the user is able to sign in to the company's application portal but
 cannot access a specific SaaS-based tool. Which of the following would the technician most likely suggest as a next step?

options.A: Reenroll the user's mobile device to be used as an MFA token.
options.B: Use a private browsing window to avoid local session conflicts.
options.C: Bypass single sign-on by directly authenticating to the application.
options.D: Reset the device being used to factory defaults.

explanation: B (Use a private browsing window) is the quick, non-destructive test: the portal login already works, so the identity provider and credentials are fine, and a stale cookie or cached token for that single SaaS application is the likely blocker. An incognito session starts with no cached state and proves it in seconds. C (Bypassing single sign-on) defeats the control and often is not even possible for a federated app. A (Reenrolling MFA) and D (Factory reset) are wildly disproportionate for one broken app.

question: A technician verifies that a malware incident occurred on some computers in a small office. Which of the following should the technician do next?

options.D: Update the anti-malware and scan the computers.

explanation: A (Quarantine the infected systems) is next because the malware has already been verified, and isolating those machines from the network stops it spreading to the rest of the office. In the malware removal process, quarantine follows identification and precedes remediation. C (Disable System Restore) and D (Update the anti-malware and scan) come after isolation, once the systems can no longer infect others. B (Educate the end users) is the final step after everything is cleaned.

question: Which of the following is a Linux command that is used for administrative purposes?
explanation: D (su) is the Linux substitute-user command, most often used to switch to root so administrative tasks can be carried out. A (runas) is its Windows counterpart for launching a program under another account, and C (net user) is the Windows command for creating and managing local accounts. B (cmcl) is not a real command in either operating system.

question:
A user recently installed an application that accesses a database from a local server. When launching the application, it does not populate any
 information. Which of the following command-line tools is the best to troubleshoot the issue?
explanation: C (netstat) lists active connections and listening ports, so the technician can see whether the application actually opened a session to the database server's port or whether the connection is being refused or never attempted. That is the heart of a client that launches but returns no data. A (ipconfig) only reports local addressing, B (nslookup) tests DNS resolution alone, and D (curl) is aimed at HTTP endpoints rather than a database socket on a local server.

question:
A small office reported a phishing attack that resulted in a malware infection. A technician is investigating the incident and has verified the
 following:
 All endpoints are updated and have the newest EDR signatures.
 Logs confirm that the malware was quarantined by EDR on one system.
 The potentially infected machine was reimaged.
 Which of the following actions should the technician take next?

options.A: Install network security tools to prevent downloading infected files from the internet.
options.B: Discuss the cause of the issue and educate the end user about security hygiene.
options.C: Flash the firmware of the router to ensure the integrity of network traffic.
options.D: Suggest alternate preventative controls that would include more advanced security software.

explanation: B (Discuss the cause and educate the end user) is next because the technical work is already finished: the EDR quarantined the malware and the affected machine was reimaged, so what remains is addressing the phishing email that started it. End-user education is the closing step of the malware removal process. A (Network security tools) and D (More advanced security software) propose spending before the human root cause is addressed, and C (Flashing router firmware) has nothing to do with a phishing infection.

question: Which of the following describes a vulnerability that has been exploited before a patch or remediation is available?
explanation: D (Zero-day) describes a flaw attacked before the vendor has issued a fix, leaving defenders zero days of warning and no patch to apply. A (Spoofing) is faking an identity such as a source address, sender or MAC. B (Brute-force) is guessing credentials by exhaustive attempts against a known login, and C (DoS) floods a service to make it unavailable. None of those depend on an unpatched flaw being unknown.

question: A help desk technician is setting up speech recognition on a Windows system. Which of the following settings should the technician use?
explanation: D (Ease of Access) is the accessibility hub in Windows Settings, holding Narrator, Magnifier, high contrast and speech recognition, which is where voice control is turned on and trained. A (Time and Language) covers region, keyboard layouts and the speech language and voice used for input, not the recognition feature itself. B (Personalization) handles themes, wallpaper and the taskbar, and C (System) holds display, sound, notifications and power.

question:
A user receives a new personal computer but is unable to run an application. An error displays saying that .NET Framework 3.5 is required and not
 found. Which of the following actions is the best way to resolve this issue?

options.A: Resolve the dependency through the "Turn Windows features on or off" menu.
options.B: Download the dependency via a third-party repository.
options.C: Ignore the dependency and install the latest version 4 instead.
options.D: Forward the trouble ticket to the SOC team because the issue poses a great security risk.

explanation: A is correct because .NET Framework 3.5 ships with Windows as an optional feature, so enabling it under Turn Windows features on or off installs it from Windows Update using Microsoft's own binaries. C (Installing version 4 instead) fails because 3.5 and 4.x install side by side and an application built for 3.5 will not run on 4 alone. B (A third-party repository) risks tampered files when the vendor supplies it natively, and D (Escalating to the SOC) treats a routine dependency as a security incident.

question:
An employee is using a photo editing program. Certain features are disabled and require a log-in, which the employee does not have. Which of the
 following is a way to resolve this issue?
explanation: A (License assignment) is the fix, because the greyed-out features are premium capabilities gated behind an entitlement tied to a user account, so an administrator needs to assign a seat or licence to that employee. C (Application repair) and D (Program reinstallation) replace damaged files, but nothing is corrupt here, the software works and simply is not entitled. B (VPN connection) would only matter for reaching an internal licence server, which is not what the prompt describes.

question:
A technician is deploying mobile devices and needs to prevent access to sensitive data if the devices are lost. Which of the following is the best
 way to prevent unauthorized access if the user is unaware that the phone is lost?
explanation: A (Encryption) is the answer because full-device encryption protects the data the moment the phone leaves the user's hands, with no action needed from anyone, which is essential when nobody yet knows the device is missing. B (Remote wipe) only works once the loss is reported and the phone is powered on and reachable. C (Geofencing) enforces location-based policy rather than protecting stored data, and D (Facial recognition) guards the lock screen but not the storage if the chip is read directly.

question: Which of the following is the quickest way to move from Windows 10 to Windows 11 without losing data?
explanation: D (In-place upgrade) runs Windows 11 setup over the existing installation and keeps files, applications and settings intact, which is both the fastest and the only listed option that preserves data. C (Clean install) wipes the drive and forces you to reinstall everything, and B (Image deployment) likewise overwrites the disk with a prepared image and is aimed at bulk rollouts. A (gpupdate) simply refreshes Group Policy and has nothing to do with upgrading an OS.

question:
Technicians are failing to document user contact information, device asset tags, and a clear description of each issue in the ticketing system.
 Which of the following should a help desk management team implement for technicians to use on every call?
explanation: C (Standard operating procedures) define the step-by-step process every technician follows on every call, including which fields must be captured, so consistency stops depending on individual habits. B (Call categories) classify what a ticket is about but never enforce collecting contact details or asset tags. A (Service-level agreements) set response and resolution targets with the customer, and D (Knowledge base articles) document fixes for known issues rather than how to log a ticket.

question:
An application's performance is degrading over time. The application is slowing, but it never gives an error and does not crash. Which of the
 following tools should a technician use to start troubleshooting?
explanation: C (Resource monitor) shows live per-process CPU, memory, disk and network usage, which is where a gradual slowdown reveals itself as a memory leak, runaway handle count or disk saturation. A (Reliability history) charts crashes, hangs and error events, and the application produces none, so it has nothing to report. B (Computer management) is a console of administrative snap-ins rather than a performance tool, and D (Disk defragment) is a maintenance action taken after a cause is identified, not a diagnostic.

question: Which of the following filesystem types does the Linux OS use?
explanation: C (ext4) is the standard journaling filesystem for most Linux distributions, supporting large volumes, extents and journaling for crash recovery. D (NTFS) is the native Windows filesystem, readable on Linux but not its default. B (APFS) is Apple's filesystem for macOS and iOS, and A (exFAT) is a lightweight cross-platform format designed for flash media and large files, with no journaling or permissions.

question: Which of the following methods would make data unrecoverable but allow the drive to be repurposed?
explanation: C (Performing a low-level format) rewrites every block on the drive, so the previous data cannot be recovered while the disk itself stays healthy and can be reissued. D (Degaussing the device) destroys the magnetic servo information along with the data, leaving a drive that can never be used again. A (Deleting the partitions) only clears the partition table, so file data remains and is trivially recoverable, and B (Implementing EFS) encrypts new files but leaves existing content in place.

question:
After a recent mobile OS upgrade to a smartphone, a user attempts to access their corporate email, but the application does not open. A
 technician restarts the smartphone, but the issue persists. Which of the following is the most likely way to resolve the issue?

options.B: Registering the smartphone with an MDM solution

explanation: A (Updating the failed software) is most likely, because a mobile OS upgrade often breaks an older app build, and installing the current version from the app store restores compatibility with the new APIs. A restart has already ruled out a transient glitch. D (Clearing the cache partition) is an Android recovery procedure for boot and update problems, not one app. C (A third-party client) is a workaround that sidesteps the real fix, and B (MDM enrollment) does nothing about a version mismatch.

question:
Users are reporting that an unsecured network is broadcasting with the same name as the normal wireless network. They are able to access the
 internet but cannot connect to the file share servers. Which of the following best describes this issue?
explanation: D (Rogue wireless access point) fits precisely: an unauthorised AP is broadcasting the legitimate SSID, so clients associate with it, reach the internet through the attacker's own uplink, but have no route to the internal file servers. That split symptom is the giveaway. A (Unreachable DNS server) would break internet browsing too. B (VLAN misconfiguration) and C (Incorrect IP address) are internal faults and neither would create a second, unsecured network with the same name.

question:
A computer technician is implementing a solution to support a new internet browsing policy for a customer's business. The policy prohibits users
 from accessing unauthorized websites based on categorization. Which of the following should the technician configure on the SOHO router?
explanation: C (Content filtering) is the SOHO router feature that blocks sites by category, matching requested URLs against lists such as gambling, social media or adult content, which is exactly how the policy is written. D (Firewall) filters on ports, protocols and addresses, so it cannot reason about site categories. B (Group Policy Editor) is a Windows domain tool with no presence on a router, and A (Secure management access) protects the router's own admin interface.

question:
Recently, the number of users sharing smartphone passcodes has increased. The management team wants a technician to deploy a more secure
 screen lock method. Which of the following technologies should the technician use?
explanation: B (Facial recognition) is biometric, so authentication is bound to the person and cannot simply be told to a colleague the way a passcode can, which directly stops the sharing problem. A (Pattern lock) is still a shared secret and is easy to shoulder surf or read from smudges on the screen. C (Device encryption) protects data at rest but is not a screen lock method, and D (Multifactor authentication) is not how a phone's lock screen is configured.

question:
An end user's laptop is having network drive connectivity issues in the office. The end user submits a help desk ticket, and a support technician is
 able to establish a remote connection and fix the issue. The following day, however, the network drive is disconnected again. Which of the
 following should the technician do next?

options.A: Connect remotely to the user’s computer to see whether the network drive is still connected.
options.B: Send documentation about how to fix the issue in case it reoccurs.
options.C: Escalate the ticket to the next level.
options.D: Keep the ticket open until next day, then close the ticket.

explanation: C (Escalate the ticket to the next level) is right because the applied fix did not hold, which means the root cause is beyond what the first-line technician diagnosed and a higher tier needs to investigate. A (Reconnecting remotely to check the drive) simply repeats work already done and the user has already reported it disconnected. B (Sending documentation) pushes the problem onto the user instead of fixing it, and D (Holding the ticket then closing it) leaves an unresolved fault.

question: Which of the following provides information to employees, such as permitted activities when using the organization's resources?
explanation: A (AUP) is the acceptable use policy, the document telling employees what they may and may not do with company computers, networks, email and internet access. D (EULA) is the licence agreement between a software vendor and whoever installs the product. B (MNDA) is a mutual non-disclosure agreement covering confidential information between parties, and C (DRM) is the technology that restricts copying and playback of protected content.

question: A technician needs to install an operating system on a large number of workstations. Which of the following is the fastest method?
explanation: D (Image deployment) is fastest at scale because a single prepared and sysprepped image is pushed to many machines at once, typically over the network, with no setup wizard to sit through on each one. A (Physical media) means walking a disc or USB stick round every workstation. B (Mountable ISO) still runs an attended installation per device, and C (Manual installation) is the slowest option of all.

question:
A user is working from home and is unable to access work files on a company laptop. Which of the following should a technician configure to fix
 the network access issue?
explanation: D (Virtual private network) builds an encrypted tunnel from the home laptop into the corporate network, so internal file shares and mapped drives resolve and authenticate as though the user were in the office. B (Wireless network) and A (Wide-area network) connectivity clearly already exists, since the laptop is online at home. C (Proxy network settings) direct web browsing through an intermediary and do nothing for access to internal SMB shares.

question:
A technician is troubleshooting an issue in which a service runs momentarily and stops at certain points in the process. The technician needs to
 determine the root cause of this issue. Which of the following tools should the technician use?
explanation: A (Event Viewer) records service start, stop and failure entries with timestamps and error codes under the System and Application logs, so the technician can read back exactly why the service terminated after the fact. B (Task Manager) and D (Process Explorer) show only what is running at this instant, and a service that has already stopped has vanished from both. C (Internet Options) configures browser security zones and proxies and is irrelevant here.

question: Which of the following is an example of an application publisher including undisclosed additional software in an installation package?
explanation: C (Potentially unwanted program) covers bundleware, the extra toolbars, trialware or search hijackers quietly packaged with a legitimate installer and buried in the fine print. It is unwanted rather than outright malicious. D (Trojan) disguises genuinely malicious code as a useful program, A (Virus) attaches to files and self-replicates, and B (Ransomware) encrypts data and demands payment. None of those describe a publisher legally bundling extras.

question: A technician needs to map a shared drive from a command-line interface. Which of the following commands should the technician use?
explanation: C (net use) is the Windows command that maps a drive letter to a network share, for example net use Z: \\server\share, and it can also list or disconnect existing mappings. A (pathping) and D (tracert) trace the path to a destination and report latency or packet loss along the hops. B (nslookup) queries DNS to resolve names to addresses. All three are diagnostic and none of them attach a share.

question:
A help desk team was alerted that a company-owned cell phone has an unrecognized password-cracking application. Which of the following
 should the help desk team do to prevent further unauthorized installations from occurring?
explanation: D (Deploy MDM) is the preventive control for mobile devices, since mobile device management can enforce app allow and block lists, restrict installation sources and remotely remove or wipe unapproved software from company-owned phones. A (Configure Group Policy) applies to domain-joined Windows machines, not smartphones. B (Implement PAM) governs privileged account usage rather than app installs, and C (Anti-malware software) might flag a tool after the fact but does not stop it being installed.

question: Which of the following is used in addition to a password to implement MFA?

options.A: Sending a code to the user's phone
options.B: Verifying the user's date of birth
options.C: Prompting the user to solve a simple math problem
options.D: Requiring the user to enter a PIN

explanation: A (Sending a code to the user's phone) adds something you have to the password's something you know, and two distinct factor types is what makes authentication multifactor. B (Date of birth) and D (PIN) are both knowledge factors, so pairing either with a password is still single-factor, just two secrets. C (Solving a math problem) is a bot check in the vein of CAPTCHA and proves nothing about who the user is.

question:
A technician is preparing to replace the batteries in rack-mounted UPS system. After ensuring the power is turned off and the batteries are fully
 discharged, the technician needs to remove the battery modules from the bottom of the rack. Which of the following steps should the technician
 take?

options.A: Ensure the fire suppression system is ready to be activated.
options.B: Use appropriate lifting techniques and guidelines.
options.C: Place the removed batteries in an antistatic bag.
options.D: Wear a face mask to filter out any harmful fumes.

explanation: B (Use appropriate lifting techniques and guidelines) is the relevant safety step, because UPS battery modules are extremely heavy, and lifting from the bottom of a rack means bending, so the technician should lift with the legs and get help or a lift cart. C (Antistatic bags) protect circuit boards from ESD, which sealed batteries do not need. D (A face mask) matters only with a leaking or damaged cell, and A (Fire suppression) is not a step in a planned, powered-down swap.

question:
A technician is setting up a surveillance system for a customer. The customer wants access to the system's web interface on the LAN via the
 system’s IP address. Which of the following should the technician use to prevent external log-in attempts from the internet?
explanation: A (Port mapping) is the router setting that decides which internal services are published through the WAN interface, so leaving the camera system's web port unmapped means it stays reachable on the LAN only and the internet has no path to its login page. B (Subnetting) divides the internal network but does not govern inbound exposure. C (Static IP) just keeps the address consistent, and D (Content filtering) restricts what internal users can browse to, not what reaches them.

question:
A technician needs to configure laptops so that only administrators can enable virtualization technology if needed. Which of the following should
 the technician configure?
explanation: A (BIOS password) is correct because virtualization support, VT-x on Intel or AMD-V, is a firmware setting, and a supervisor password on BIOS/UEFI setup means only staff who know it can enter the menu and toggle it. B (Guest account), C (Screen lock) and D (AutoRun setting) all live inside the operating system and take effect long after firmware setup has run, so none of them can stop a user changing a BIOS option at boot.

question: Which of the following file types would a desktop support technician most likely use to automate tasks for a Windows user log-in?
explanation: A (.bat) is the batch file, interpreted natively by cmd.exe on every Windows installation, which makes it the standard choice for drive mappings, printer connections and other logon script tasks. B (.sh) is a shell script for Linux and macOS and will not execute on Windows without a compatibility layer. C (.py) requires the Python interpreter to be installed, and D (.js) is aimed at browsers or Node, neither of which is guaranteed on a corporate desktop.

question:
A technician uses AI to draft a proposal about the benefits of new software. When reading the draft, the technician notices that the draft contains
 factually incorrect information. Which of the following best describes this scenario?
explanation: B (Hallucinations) is the term for a generative model producing confident but fabricated output, because it predicts plausible-sounding text rather than checking facts, which is why AI drafts always need verifying. D (Plagiarism) is presenting someone else's work as your own, a different failure. A (Data privacy) concerns feeding confidential material into the model, and C (Appropriate use) is the policy question of whether AI should be used for the task in the first place.

question:
Which of the following describes an attack in which an attacker sets up a rogue AP that tricks users into connecting to the rogue AP instead of the
 legitimate network?
explanation: B (Evil twin) is an attack in which a rogue access point advertises the same SSID as the real network, often with a stronger signal, so victims associate with it and the attacker can intercept or manipulate their traffic. D (Shoulder surfing) is watching someone type a password or PIN. C (Tailgating) is following an authorised person through a secured door, and A (Stalkerware) is monitoring software installed on a device to track its owner.

question:
A user is experiencing issues with outdated images while browsing websites. Which of the following settings should a technician use to correct
 this issue?
explanation: C (Internet Options) is the Control Panel applet that controls Temporary Internet Files; deleting the browsing cache forces the browser to pull current images from the server instead of serving stale copies from disk. A (Administrative Tools) holds system consoles like Services and Event Viewer, and D (Ease of Access) covers accessibility. B (Windows Defender Firewall) filters traffic and would block pages entirely rather than show old versions of them.

question:
Every time a user loads a specific spreadsheet, their computer is temporarily unresponsive. The user also notices that the title bar indicates the
 applications are not responding. Which of the following would a technician most likely inspect?

options.C: Bandwidth status as reported in the Task Manager
options.D: File size and related memory utilization

explanation: D (File size and related memory utilization) is right because a workbook is loaded entirely into RAM; a spreadsheet that has grown large enough forces heavy paging to disk, which is what freezes the machine and produces the not responding title bar. A (Anti-malware logs) is unlikely when the hang reproduces only with one specific file. C misreads Task Manager, which reports network throughput, and a local spreadsheet does not depend on it.

question:
A user frequently misplaces their Windows laptop and is concerned about it being stolen. The user would like additional security controls on their
 laptop. Which of the following is a built-in technology that a technician can use to enable full drive encryption?
explanation: D (BitLocker) is the encryption feature built into Windows Pro and Enterprise that encrypts the entire volume, usually sealed to the TPM, so a thief who removes the drive gets nothing readable. C (Encrypting File System) is also native but only encrypts selected files and folders, leaving the rest of the volume in the clear. B (NTFS) is the file system EFS relies on, and A (Active Directory) is a directory service, not encryption.

question: Which of the following is used to apply corporate restrictions on an Apple device?
explanation: D (Management profile) is the payload an MDM server pushes to an iPhone, iPad or Mac to enforce corporate settings such as passcode rules, restrictions and Wi-Fi or VPN configuration. C (Apple ID) is the user's personal account and cannot carry corporate policy. A (App Store) distributes software, and B (VPN configuration) only affects how traffic is routed; neither applies restrictions to the device.

question:
A user's new smartphone is not staying charged throughout the day. The smartphone charges fully every night. Which of the following should a
 technician review first to troubleshoot the issue?
explanation: D (Background applications) is the first thing to check because apps that keep syncing, refreshing location or polling in the background drain a battery steadily through the day even though it started at full charge. A (Storage usage) hurts free space and performance, not runtime. C (Charger wattage) would show up as slow charging, but the phone already charges fully overnight, and B (End of software support) has no bearing on a new device.

question:
A customer is unable to open some files on their system. Each time the customer attempts to open a file, the customer receives a message that
 the file is encrypted. Which of the following best describes this issue?
explanation: B (Ransomware) encrypts the victim's files and blocks access until a payment is made, which matches the encrypted-file message appearing every time a document is opened. D (Cryptominer) quietly consumes CPU and GPU cycles but leaves files usable. A (Keylogger) captures keystrokes, and C (Phishing) is a social engineering delivery method rather than the payload that locks the data.

question:
An organization is experiencing an increased number of issues. A technician notices applications that are not installed by default. Users are
 reporting an increased number of system prompts for software licensing. Which of the following would the security team most likely do to
 remediate the root cause?

options.A: Deploy an internal PKI to filter encrypted web traffic.
options.B: Remove users from the local admin group.
options.C: Implement stronger controls to block suspicious websites.
options.D: Enable stricter UAC settings on Windows.

explanation: B (Remove users from the local admin group) attacks the root cause: unapproved applications and licensing prompts appear because users hold administrator rights and can install whatever they like. D (Enable stricter UAC settings) only adds a consent prompt that a local admin can approve anyway. C (Block suspicious websites) and A (Deploy an internal PKI) address one delivery path but leave the underlying install privilege intact.

question:
A support specialist needs to decide whether to install a 32-bit or 64-bit OS architecture on a new computer. Which of the following specifications
 will help the specialist determine which OS architecture to use?
explanation: A (16GB RAM) is the deciding specification because a 32-bit operating system can address only about 4GB of memory, so 16GB installed can only be used by a 64-bit build. B (Intel i7 CPU) names a processor family but the amount of usable memory is what forces the decision here. C (500GB HDD) is storage capacity and D (1Gbps Ethernet) is network speed, neither of which has any relationship to OS architecture. (Note: the dump prints B as the answer, but the highest-voted community discussion says A — we go with the community.)

question: Which of the following prevents forced entry into a building?
explanation: D (Bollard) is a solid post set into the ground that physically stops a vehicle from ramming a door or storefront, which is what prevents forced entry. B (Motion-activated lighting) and C (Video surveillance) are deterrent and detective controls that record or discourage an intruder but stop nothing. A (PIV card) authenticates an authorized person at a reader and does nothing against someone who forces the door.

question: A technician is assigned to offboard a user. Which of the following are common tasks on an offboarding checklist? (Choose two.)

options.A: Quarantine the hard drive in the user's laptop.
options.B: Deactivate the user's key fobs for door access.
options.C: Purge all PII associated with the user.
options.E: Turn off the network ports underneath the user’s desk.
options.F: Add the MAC address of the user's computer to a blocklist.

explanation: B (Deactivate the user's key fobs) removes physical building access the moment the person leaves, and D (Suspend the user's email account) blocks logon while preserving the mailbox for retention or a manager's access. A (Quarantine the hard drive) applies only to investigations or litigation holds, and C (Purge all PII) usually conflicts with retention requirements. E and F, disabling desk ports and blocklisting a MAC, are not standard offboarding items.

question:
A company would like to deploy baseline images to new computers as they are started up on the network. Which of the following boot processes
 should the company use for this task?
explanation: D (PXE) lets the network card request an address and download a boot image from a deployment server the moment the machine powers on, which is exactly how baseline images get pushed to new computers at scale. C (USB) requires a technician to walk to every machine with media. A (ISO) is an image file format rather than a boot process, and B (Secure boot) validates firmware signatures instead of delivering an image.

question:
A user has been adding data to the same spreadsheet for several years. After adding a significant amount of data, they are now unable to open
 the file. Which of the following should a technician do to resolve the issue?

options.A: Revert the spreadsheet to the last restore point.

explanation: B (Increase the amount of RAM) is right because the spreadsheet application has to load the whole workbook into memory, and years of added rows have pushed it past what the machine can hold, so the file simply will not open. C (Defragment the storage drive) speeds up mechanical seek times but does not create memory. A (Restore point) reverts the OS rather than repairing a file, and D (Network speed) is irrelevant to a local document.

question:
A technician installs VPN client software that has a software bug from the vendor. After the vendor releases an update to the software, the
 technician attempts to reinstall the software but keeps getting an error message that the network adapter for the VPN already exists. Which of the
 following should the technician do next to mitigate this issue?

options.A: Run the latest OS security updates.
options.B: Map the network adapter to the new software.

explanation: D (Delete hidden network adapters) is the fix because the old VPN install left its virtual adapter registered in the system; showing hidden devices in Device Manager and removing the ghost entry lets the new package create its own. C (Update the network adapter's firmware) targets the physical NIC, which is not the adapter causing the conflict. A (OS security updates) will not clear a stale device record, and there is no facility to remap an adapter as B suggests.

question:
Which of the following is the best reason for a network engineering team to provide a help desk technician with IP addressing information to use
 on workstations being deployed in a secure network segment?

options.A: Only specific DNS servers are allowed outbound access.
options.B: The network allow list is set to a specific address.
options.C: DHCP services are not enabled for this subnet.
options.D: NAC servers only allow for security updates to be installed.

explanation: C (DHCP services are not enabled for this subnet) explains why the workstations need addressing details handed over manually: with no DHCP scope on the secure segment, each host must be configured with a static IP, mask, gateway and DNS. B (Network allow list) and A (DNS restrictions) control what traffic is permitted once a host is addressed, not how it obtains an address. D (NAC servers) governs admission and remediation, not IP assignment.

question:
A technician is using a credential manager to safeguard a large number of credentials. Which of the following is important for using this
 application?
explanation: B (Secure master password) matters most because the entire vault is encrypted with that one credential, so its strength determines whether every stored password is protected or exposed. C (TPM module) can add hardware-backed key storage but is not required by most credential managers. A (Restricted log-in times) and D (Windows lock screen) are operating system controls that do nothing to protect the vault file itself if it is copied elsewhere.

question: Which of the following methods involves requesting a user's approval via a push notification to verify the user's identity?
explanation: B (Authenticator) apps such as Microsoft or Google Authenticator send a push to the enrolled phone that the user approves or denies, which is the method described. D (SMS) and A (Call) deliver a one-time code by text or voice that the user must type in, with no approval prompt. C (Hardware token) generates or stores a code on a physical device and has no data connection to receive a push.

question:
A customer wants to be able to work from home but does not want to be responsible for bringing company equipment back and forth. Which of
 the following would allow the user to remotely access and use a Windows PC at the main office? (Choose two.)
explanation: D (VPN) puts the home laptop on the corporate network with an encrypted tunnel, and C (RDP) then opens an interactive session on the office Windows PC using port 3389, so the user works on company equipment without carrying it home. B (SSH) gives only a command line and is uncommon on Windows desktops, F (WinRM) is for remote management commands rather than a desktop, A (SPICE) targets virtual machines, and E (RMM) is an administrator's management platform.

question:
A company wants to use a single operating system for its workstation and servers and avoid licensing fees. Which of the following operating
 systems would the company most likely select?
explanation: A (Linux) is free and open source with distributions built for both desktops and servers, so one operating system covers workstations and servers with no licensing cost. B (Windows) requires per-device and per-server client access licensing, and C (macOS) is licensed only for Apple hardware and has no current server platform. D (Chrome OS) is a lightweight client OS with no server edition at all.

question:
A user is attempting to open on a mobile phone a HD video that is hosted on a popular media streaming website. The user is receiving connection
 timeout errors. The mobile reception icon area is showing two bars next to 3G. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the issue?

options.A: The user does not have Wi-Fi enabled.
options.B: The website's subscription has run out.
options.C: The bandwidth is not fast enough.
options.D: The mobile device storage is full.

explanation: C (The bandwidth is not fast enough) fits the symptoms: two bars on 3G cannot sustain the throughput an HD stream needs, so the connection stalls and times out. A (Wi-Fi not enabled) is not required since cellular data is clearly connected. D (Storage full) would produce a save or download error rather than a connection timeout, and B (Subscription ran out) would return an account or payment message from the site.

question:
A technician notices that the weekly backup is taking too long to complete. The daily backups are incremental. Which of the following would most
 likely resolve the issue?
explanation: D (Running synthetic full weekly backups) solves it because the backup server merges the last full backup with the accumulated incrementals on the backup storage itself, producing a new full without re-reading everything from production. A (Changing the backup window) just moves the same long job. B (Weekly incrementals) would leave no full backup to restore from, and C (More storage) adds capacity without shortening the read time.

question:
A help desk technician needs to remove RAM from retired workstations and upgrade other workstations that have applications that use more
 memory with this RAM. Which of the following actions would the technician most likely take?

options.B: Use antistatic bags for storage and transport.
options.C: Plug in the power supply to ground each workstation.

explanation: B (Use antistatic bags for storage and transport) is right because memory modules are highly susceptible to electrostatic discharge, and the shielded bag is what protects them between the retired machine and the target workstation. D (Install memory in identical pairs) matters when populating dual-channel slots but is not the handling action asked about. A (Demagnetize memory) does nothing to semiconductor chips, and C is unsafe advice; the system should be unplugged and the technician grounded with a strap.

question:
A customer’s computer does not have an active connection to the network. A technician goes through a few troubleshooting steps but is unable to
 resolve the issue. The technician has exhausted their knowledge. The customer expresses frustration at the time taken to resolve this issue.
 Which of the following should the technician do?

options.A: Escalate the issue to a senior team member and provide next steps to the customer.
options.B: Dismiss the customer and reschedule another troubleshooting session at a later date.
options.C: Interrupt the customer and express that troubleshooting support tickets can take time.
options.D: Maintain a positive attitude and continue to ask questions regarding the scope of the issue.

explanation: A (Escalate the issue and provide next steps) is correct because the technician has run out of technical options, and professional practice is to hand the ticket to someone with deeper knowledge while telling the frustrated customer exactly what happens next. B (Dismiss the customer) and C (Interrupt the customer) both break basic customer service rules about listening and not being dismissive. D (Keep asking scope questions) simply stalls when the technician already has nothing left to try.

question:
A company executive is currently attending a major music festival with a large number of attendees and is having trouble accessing a work email
 account. The email application is not downloading emails and also appears to become stuck during connection attempts. Which of the following
 is most likely causing the disruption?

options.A: The phone has no storage space available.
options.B: Company firewalls are configured to block remote access to email resources.
options.C: Too many devices in the same area are trying to connect to the mobile network.
options.D: The festival organizer prohibits internet usage during the event and has blocked the internet signal.

explanation: C (Too many devices trying to connect to the mobile network) is the likely cause because a festival crowd saturates the local cell towers, so sessions stall part way through and the mail client never finishes syncing. A (No storage space) produces a specific storage warning rather than a hung connection. B (Company firewalls blocking remote access) would have broken email everywhere, not just at the venue, and D describes something festival organizers cannot legally do.

question:
A company recently transitioned to a cloud-based productivity suite and wants to secure the environment from external threat actors. Which of the
 following is the most effective method?
explanation: A (Multifactor authentication) is the most effective control because external attacks on cloud suites almost always start with stolen or guessed credentials, and a second factor makes a harvested password useless. D (Strong passwords) still leaves a single factor that can be phished or reused. B (Encryption) protects data at rest and in transit but not an account an attacker logs into legitimately, and C (Backups) is a recovery measure after the fact.

question:
A user reports getting a BSOD error on their computer at least twice a day. Which of the following should the technician use to determine the
 cause?
explanation: A (Event Viewer) is where Windows records the bug check stop code, the timestamp and often the faulting driver for each blue screen, which is what identifies the cause of a repeating crash. B (Performance Monitor) tracks live resource counters and will not tell you why the system halted. C (System Information) lists hardware and configuration details, and D (Device Manager) shows current device status but keeps no crash history.

question:
A technician is setting up a Windows server to allow remote desktop connections for multiple users. Which of the following should the technician
 configure on the workstation?
explanation: C (User Accounts) is correct because allowing several people to connect requires adding each of them to the Remote Desktop Users group; without that membership the connection is refused even with the service running. A (Firewall) rules for TCP 3389 are opened automatically when Remote Desktop is enabled. B (Computer Management) is a console that contains other tools rather than the setting itself, and D (Ease of Access) covers accessibility options. (Note: the dump prints A as the answer, but the highest-voted community discussion says C — we go with the community.) Worth flagging: B (Computer Management) has a real claim, since adding several users to the Remote Desktop Users group is done through the Local Users and Groups snap-in.

question:
A technician thinks that an application a user downloaded from the internet may not be the legitimate one, even though the name is the same. The
 technician needs to confirm whether the application is legitimate. Which of the following should the technician do?

options.A: Compare the hash value from the vendor.
options.B: Run Task Manager and compare the process ID.
options.C: Run the application in safe mode.
options.D: Verify the file name is correct.

explanation: A (Compare the hash value from the vendor) is the reliable check: running the downloaded file through SHA-256 or MD5 and matching it to the checksum the vendor publishes proves the bytes were not altered, since any tampering changes the digest. D (Verify the file name) is worthless because a name is trivially copied, which is the whole premise here. B (Compare the process ID) uses a number assigned at random each run, and C (Safe mode) proves nothing about authenticity.

question:
A technician must map a network drive on a piece of legacy equipment running an end-of-life OS. Which of the following is the best script to map
 the drive using simple Windows commands?
explanation: B (Batch) is the best fit because a .bat file runs native Windows commands such as net use directly from the command interpreter, and that interpreter exists on every Windows version including an end-of-life one, with no runtime to install. A (Shell) scripts are written for Unix and Linux shells. C (VB) script is heavier and being deprecated, and D (Java) requires a JRE the legacy machine probably does not have.

question:
After clicking on an advertisement, a user reports that their browser is slow. A technician looks at the network connections for the machine and
 notices a large number of outbound connections. Which of the following actions should the technician take next?
explanation: D (Quarantine the system) comes next because the heavy outbound connections after a malicious ad point to an active infection, and the incident response order is to contain the host before cleaning it, so it stops beaconing or spreading. B (Run antivirus scans) is the eradication step that follows quarantine. C (Reboot the computer) can destroy volatile evidence without stopping the traffic, and A (Enable the firewall) is far too late to help now.

question:
Various alerts on a user’s Windows 11 laptop are continually interrupting the user during videoconference calls. Which of the following should a
 support technician recommend to best solve the issue?

options.A: Use multiple sound output devices for the various source applications.
options.B: Disable all notifications in different applications in the order they appear.
options.C: Configure the Sounds option in Control Panel to be set to No Sounds.
options.D: Set Windows Notifications settings to Do Not Disturb.

explanation: D (Set Windows Notifications settings to Do Not Disturb) is the single Windows 11 setting that suppresses banners and their sounds during a call and can be scheduled or triggered automatically, then released afterwards. B (Disable notifications per application) means hunting through every app and still misses new ones. C (No Sounds scheme) silences audio but the pop-ups keep covering the screen, and A (Multiple sound output devices) has nothing to do with alerts.

question:
Company employees do not have assigned workspaces and regularly work at different computers and physical locations. Which of the following
 should the company implement to maintain data security and minimize the amount of user data that needs to be transferred?
explanation: D (Roaming profiles) stores the user's profile on a server and loads it wherever they log on, so settings and documents follow them between machines while the data stays centrally held and only the delta is copied. C (Portable drives) puts company data on removable media that is easily lost. A (Centralized certificate storage) handles authentication material only, and B (Cloud email) covers messaging but not the desktop profile or files.

question:
A user downloads an application with a plug-in that is designed to automatically prompt for an OTP when the user browses to a specific website.
 The plug-in installs without any warnings or errors. The first time the user goes to the site, the prompt does not open, and the user cannot access
 the site. Which of the following browser settings should the user configure?
explanation: A (Extensions/add-ins) is where a browser plug-in lives, and it must be enabled and granted permission for that site before it can hook the page and raise the OTP prompt; installing without error does not mean the browser activated it. B (Certificate validity) issues would show a security warning instead. C (Proxy settings) would break browsing generally, and D (Trusted sources) governs where installs may come from, which already succeeded.

question:
A technician needs to install a home wireless router for a customer who wants to limit connections made to the network from the internet. Which
 of the following should the technician do?
explanation: D (Disable UPnP) is the right move because UPnP lets internal devices punch inbound port forwards through the router's firewall automatically, which is precisely how connections get opened from the internet side. B (Change the default password) protects the router's admin interface but leaves those automatic forwards in place. A (Content filtering) restricts which sites users reach outbound, and C (SSID settings) only affects the local wireless name and visibility.

question:
A technician is installing a cloud-based productivity suite and keeps getting an error message stating that the installation is unavailable. Which of
 the following troubleshooting steps should the technician try first?
explanation: C (Checking the license device limit) is the first check because subscription productivity suites cap how many devices one account may activate, and exceeding it returns exactly this kind of unavailable message. A (Reinstalling the suite) repeats the same activation call and the same error. D (Updating the device OS) is a plausible later step but not the first, and B (Downloading an open-source alternative) abandons the problem rather than troubleshooting it.

question: A user wants to dispose of a failed hard drive in a way that ensures the data is unrecoverable. Which of the following is the best at-home method?
explanation: E (Drilling) is the practical at-home option: putting several holes through the platters or flash chips with an ordinary power drill makes the media physically unreadable. C (Shredding) and D (Degaussing) both destroy data effectively but need industrial equipment or a disposal service, so they are not at-home methods. A (Standard formatting) only clears the file table and B (Low-level formatting) requires a functioning drive, which this one is not.

question:
A customer's laptop will not turn on. The customer is distraught and panicking because the laptop contains family pictures that can never be
 replaced. Which of the following communication techniques is most important for the technician to demonstrate in this situation?

options.A: The technician should provide the customer with the appropriate SLA agreement.
options.B: The technician should inform the customer about replacement options for an increased cost.
options.C: The technician should project confidence and maintain a positive attitude.
options.D: The technician should be dressed in appropriate business casual attire to project expertise.

explanation: C (Project confidence and maintain a positive attitude) is what the situation calls for, since the customer is panicking about irreplaceable photos and needs reassurance that the problem is being handled competently. A (Provide the SLA) answers a question nobody asked and sounds like deflection. B (Offer replacement options at increased cost) reads as an upsell at the worst moment, and D (Business casual attire) is a general professionalism point, not a communication technique for this exchange.

question:
Which of the following security technologies is designed to enable security visibility and respond to traffic outside of the host and at the network
 level?
explanation: C (XDR) is extended detection and response, which correlates telemetry from endpoints, network sensors, email and cloud services into one view and can act on threats seen beyond a single host. D (Antivirus) inspects files and processes on the machine it runs on only. B (UAC) is a Windows privilege elevation prompt, and A (RADIUS) provides authentication, authorization and accounting for network access rather than threat detection.

question:
A technician completes the installation of an OS that appears to be successful. However, when the technician removes the USB drive that was
 used for the installation and restarts the system, the following error appears:
 No OS found.
 Which of the following should the technician do next to resolve the issue?

options.A: Reinstall the OS from a new ISO image.
options.B: Enable UEFI devices in the BIOS.
options.C: Restart in recovery mode and troubleshoot.
options.D: Install the storage drivers for the motherboard.

explanation: B (Enable UEFI devices in the BIOS) is next because the installation itself succeeded, so the drive holds a valid OS; the firmware is simply not set to boot the UEFI entry the installer created, leaving it with nothing bootable once the USB is gone. A (Reinstall from a new ISO) repeats work that already completed cleanly. D (Storage drivers) would have been needed during setup, and E (Reseat the SATA cable) is ruled out since the installer wrote to that disk.

question:
An employee is trying to connect their company laptop to an airport’s Wi-Fi during a business trip. Once the network is connected, a pop-up
 window appears with the airport logo, which the employee quickly closes. The internet connection is not working properly, and the employee
 cannot access any websites. Which of the following should a help desk technician suggest to the employee?

options.A: Look for a wall socket with RJ45 and try to connect the laptop to it.
options.C: Tell the employee that company policy prohibits connection to public Wi-Fi.
options.D: Reconnect to the network and read the pop-up carefully.

explanation: D (Reconnect to the network and read the pop-up carefully) is right because that window is the captive portal, and until the terms are accepted or the login is completed the network blocks all web traffic. A (Look for an RJ45 socket) is a workaround that rarely exists in a terminal. B (Contact the airport IT department) escalates something the user can fix in seconds, and C (Quote company policy) leaves the employee with no working connection at all.

question:
A technician installs a Bluetooth headset for a user. During testing, the sound is still coming from the speaker on the computer. The technician
 verifies the headset shows up in Device Manager. Which of the following would the technician most likely do to fix this issue?

options.A: Update the drivers for the wireless headset.
options.B: Replace the battery on the headset, and try again later.
options.C: Verify that the sound is not muted in the control panel.
options.D: Change the headset as the default device in sound settings.

explanation: D (Change the headset as the default device in sound settings) is the fix because Windows keeps routing playback to the previous default output even after a new device pairs successfully. A (Update the drivers) is unnecessary since the headset already enumerates properly in Device Manager. B (Replace the battery) is contradicted by the device being paired and visible, and C (Check for mute) does not fit, as sound is audible, just from the wrong output.

question: Which of the following is a protocol that provides AAA for network services?
explanation: A (RADIUS) provides authentication, authorization and accounting for network services, which is why it backs 802.1X wireless, VPN concentrators and switch port access, using UDP 1812 and 1813. B (Kerberos) authenticates users in a domain with tickets but offers no accounting layer. C (TKIP) is a legacy wireless encryption protocol, and D (WPA3) is a wireless security standard that can call on RADIUS in enterprise mode rather than providing AAA itself.

question:
A user's application only works with a legacy version of the OS. The OS is reaching its end of life date. For security reasons, the company is
 migrating to the current version of the OS. Which of the following is the most efficient way to complete the migration while maintaining
 accessibility to the application?
explanation: D (Virtualization) is the efficient answer because the legacy OS runs as a guest VM on a current, patched host, so the application keeps working while the physical machine is migrated and secured. C (Multiboot) forces a reboot every time the user switches, so both environments are never available at once. A (Terminal server) still needs the old OS hosted somewhere, and B (Bare-metal server) dedicates whole hardware to one legacy instance.

question: A technician needs to disable guest log-ins on domain-joined desktop machines. Which of the following should the technician use?
explanation: A (Group Policy) is correct for domain-joined machines, since a single GPO linked to the OU pushes the guest account setting to every desktop and reapplies it automatically. D (MSConfig) manages boot options and startup items on one local machine and cannot disable an account. C (Microsoft Management Console) is only the shell that hosts snap-ins, and B (Firewall) filters network traffic rather than controlling local logon rights.

question:
After using a third-party disk optimization software package, a technician restarts a laptop and receives the message No operating system found.
 The technician verifies that the BIOS properly recognizes the SSD. Which of the following should the technician do next?

options.A: Update BitLocker settings in the BIOS.
options.C: Turn on from installation media and repair the MBR
options.D: Isolate the system from the corporate network.

explanation: C (Turn on from installation media and repair the MBR) is next because the optimization utility corrupted the boot record while the BIOS still sees the SSD, so the hardware is healthy and only the boot code needs rebuilding with bootrec or Startup Repair. B (Replace the CMOS battery) would show up as lost time and firmware settings. A (BitLocker settings) is not indicated by the symptom, and D (Isolate the system) is a malware containment step, not a boot repair.

question: A user reports that their corporate mobile phone is lost. Which of the following protects the data locally on the phone from unauthorized access?
explanation: C (Remote wipe) is the control that protects the data sitting on a lost handset, because the MDM or find-my-device service issues a command that erases the device before anyone can get into it. A (Password manager) safeguards stored credentials but not the rest of the phone. B (Degaussing) needs physical possession and does not affect flash storage anyway, and D (Antivirus) only screens for malicious apps.

question: A user receives a push notification to approve or deny a log-in request when using MFA. Which of the following describes this security measure?
explanation: C (Authenticator application) is the mechanism behind an approve-or-deny push, as the enrolled app receives the prompt and confirms possession of the registered device. A (One-time password) is a numeric code the user reads and types, with no push involved. B (Zero Trust model) is an overall architecture rather than a specific factor, and D (Privileged access management) controls how administrative accounts are checked out and used.

question:
An administrator is investigating a technical outage. The management team wants information that includes the summary of the outage and
 actions taken. Which of the following documentation should the administrator provide to the management team?
explanation: C (Incident report) is the document management wants, since it captures the summary of what happened, the timeline, the impact and the actions taken to restore service. A (Knowledge base article) is written to help others resolve a recurring problem in future. D (Standard operating procedure) prescribes how routine work should be done, and B (Non-disclosure agreement) is a legal contract about confidentiality.

question:
A technician is troubleshooting a print spooler that repeatedly fails to start on a Windows 11 desktop computer. The technician determines the
 root cause is required dependencies are failing to run. Which of the following tools is the technician using?
explanation: B (Services) is the tool, because that is where each service's state, startup type and its dependency relationships are listed, so a spooler failing because a required dependency will not run is diagnosed there. A (Processes) shows executables and their resource usage without any dependency information. C (Startup) controls which apps launch at sign-in, and D (Performance) graphs CPU, memory and disk activity.

question:
A user’s computer is running slowly. Web pages take several seconds to open, and applications are slow responding to user input. A technician
 opens the Windows Task Manager and sees the following information:
 Disk: 2%
 Network: 12%
 GPU: 15%
 CPU: 70%
 Memory: 97%
 Which of the following would a technician most likely do to resolve the issue?
explanation: C (Close unnecessary programs) is right because memory sits at 97 percent while disk, network and GPU are barely loaded, so the machine is starved of RAM and constantly paging, which is what makes every application sluggish. A (Clear cached browser data) and D (Delete temporary files) recover disk space, and disk usage is only 2 percent. B (Upgrade the network connection) does nothing when the network is at 12 percent.

question:
A malicious actor uses multiple endpoints that are spread across multiple locations to target a single endpoint. Which of the following describes
 this threat?
explanation: D (Distributed denial of service) matches exactly: many compromised endpoints in different locations flood one target so it cannot serve legitimate requests. C (Brute-force attack) hammers credentials rather than availability and is usually from one source. A (On-path attack) positions the attacker between two communicating parties to intercept traffic, and B (SQL injection) inserts crafted statements into a database query through an application.

question:
A user decides to switch to Windows from Linux and is trying to migrate data using an external USB hard disk. However, when the user connects
 the cable to the Windows machine, an error message appears stating the device must be formatted before it can be used. The hard disk works as
 expected when connected to the Linux machine. Which of the following should the user do to resolve this issue?

options.A: Configure Windows firewall to allow data from Linux systems.
options.B: Replace the cable with Windows-supported hardware.
options.C: Apply a firmware update from the PC manufacturer.
options.D: Update the file allocation system to exFAT.

explanation: D (Update the file allocation system to exFAT) is the resolution because the disk carries a Linux file system such as ext4 that Windows cannot read, which is why it offers to format it; copying the data off on the Linux machine and reformatting to exFAT gives a volume both operating systems mount natively. A (Firewall rules) and C (Firmware update) have nothing to do with file systems, and B (Replace the cable) is ruled out since Windows already detects the drive.

question:
An end user discovers a virus on their computer. A technician quarantines the computer, scans for viruses, and remediates the infection. Which of
 the following is the next step the technician should take?
explanation: B (Educate the end user) is the final step of the malware removal process, because explaining how the infection arrived is what stops the same behaviour causing it again. A (Perform a secondary antivirus scan) belongs to the scanning and remediation phase that has already been completed. D (Review system logs) is part of identifying the symptoms earlier on, and C (Reimage the computer) is unnecessary once the infection has been successfully removed.

question:
An administrator requires information about a server to identify the product owner and whether it has any business-critical services. Which of the
 following can the administrator refer to in order to find this information?
explanation: A (CMDB) is the configuration management database, which inventories assets and records their owners, dependencies and business criticality, so it answers both parts of the question. B (SLA) defines agreed uptime and response targets between provider and customer. C (SOP) documents how a task should be carried out, and D (EULA) is the licensing agreement governing software use, none of which track ownership of a specific server.

question: An administrator must rename the administrator account on a Windows desktop. Which of the following tools is best for this task?
explanation: A (lusrmgr.msc) opens Local Users and Groups, the direct console for renaming, disabling or resetting local accounts including the built-in administrator. C (gpedit.msc) can enforce a rename through a security policy setting but is a broader policy editor rather than the right tool for a single desktop change. B (devmgmt.msc) is Device Manager for hardware and drivers, and D (eventvwr.msc) only reads logs.

question: Which of the following malware types typically has very high computing resource usage?
explanation: B (Cryptominer) is the malware that hammers CPU and GPU, since mining cryptocurrency is pure computation and the infected machine runs hot and slow while the attacker profits. A (Rootkit) works hard at staying hidden and deliberately keeps its footprint small. C (Boot sector virus) infects the MBR to load early in the boot process, and D (Trojan) describes disguised delivery rather than any particular resource profile.

question:
The battery on a user’s smartphone discharges quickly when the user travels. The smartphone was replaced two weeks ago. Which of the
 following should a technician do first?

options.A: Replace the battery with a higher capacity option.
options.B: Provide an external battery to extend the usage time.
options.C: Ensure that the charging port is working as expected.
options.D: Look for applications that are reporting the highest utilization.

explanation: D (Look for applications reporting the highest utilization) is the first step because the phone is only two weeks old, so a rogue or location-hungry app draining power while travelling is far likelier than a hardware fault, and the battery usage screen names the culprit directly. A (Replace the battery) and B (Provide an external battery) treat the symptom without diagnosing it. C (Check the charging port) does not fit, since the problem is discharge speed, not an inability to charge.

question:
A technician is securing a newly deployed workstation that only assigned users can access. Which of the following techniques should the
 technician do to prevent unauthorized users from accessing the workstation? (Choose two.)
explanation: C (Enable screensaver locks) forces re-authentication whenever the workstation is left idle, closing the easiest window for a passerby, and F (Apply the BIOS password) stops someone changing the boot order to start from external media and bypass Windows entirely. B (Enable SSH) would add a remote access path, which is the opposite of what is wanted. E (Enable the firewall) filters network traffic rather than local logon, A (Defragment) is maintenance, and D (Disable iCloud integration) is not a Windows workstation control.

question:
An international traveler is concerned about others accessing the contents of their smartphone if it is lost or stolen. The traveler has enabled
 biometrics. Which of the following additional security measures further reduces the risk of unauthorized data access?
explanation: D (Device encryption) adds real protection beyond the lock screen, because encrypted storage stays unreadable even if the flash is removed or the device is attacked offline. C (PIN code screen lock) is simply another unlock method alongside the biometrics already enabled, so it adds little. A (Remote backups) protects against data loss rather than disclosure, and B (Location tracking) helps recover the handset but does nothing to keep its contents private.

question:
A small town’s clerk wants to work from home on a town-issued laptop. The clerk needs to be able to access documents on the town hall server.
 Which of the following solutions does a technician need to set up for the clerk?
explanation: C (VPN) is what the clerk needs, since it places the town-issued laptop on the town hall network over an encrypted tunnel so the mapped server shares and documents are reachable from home. B (RDP) and A (VNC) would remote-control another desktop, which is not what was described, and exposing either directly to the internet is bad practice. D (SSH) provides a command-line session and is not how Windows file shares are accessed.

question: A company is implementing the 3-2-1 backup rule. Which of the following should the company do?

options.A: Perform both full and differential backups.
options.B: Test the backup integrity every three weeks.
options.C: Keep all backup media on site for fast recovery.
options.D: Use at least two different types of media.

explanation: D (Use at least two different types of media) is part of the rule, which calls for three copies of the data stored on two different media types with one copy kept off site. C (Keep all backup media on site) directly breaks the off-site requirement that protects against fire, flood or theft. A (Full and differential backups) describes a backup scheme, not the 3-2-1 rule, and B (Test integrity every three weeks) is sound practice but not one of the three numbers.

question:
