A team member provides a link to an online slide deck presentation so other team members can add to the presentation. The link does not work
 for any of the other team members. Which of the following should the team check first?
explanation: C (Viewing and sharing permissions) should be checked first, because cloud presentations default to owner-only access and the link fails for everyone until the file is shared with the team or the link is set to allow editing. A (Version history) shows past revisions of a file people cannot even open. B (Web browser compatibility) would not fail identically for every member, and D (License management) affects the owner's own ability to use the suite.

question:
A support technician receives a computer with a non-responsive touch pad. The touch pad does not appear to be physically damaged. Which of
 the following tools should the technician use to check the touch pad driver?
explanation: B (Device Manager) is the tool for driver work, showing the touch pad's status, error code and driver version, with options to update, roll back or reinstall it. A (System Configuration) controls boot options and startup services rather than devices. C (Event Viewer) may log a related error after the fact but does not expose the driver itself, and D (Local Users and Groups) manages accounts and has nothing to do with hardware.

question:
A user is renaming a .txt file to a .xml file. After renaming the file. Windows Explorer shows the filename as Document.xml. However, the
 document properties shows the type of file as: Text Document(.txt). Which of the following controls enables the user to correctly change the file
 type?
explanation: Windows hides known file extensions by default, so the user only renamed the visible part and the file is really Document.xml.txt, still registered as a text document. Turning off the hide-extensions setting in File Explorer's View options exposes the true extension so it can actually be changed. A (Indexing options) only affects search speed, B (Format command) wipes an entire volume, and C (Personalization) changes desktop appearance.

question:
A technician is unable to upgrade a desktop computer from Windows 10 to Windows 11. Which of the following is most likely preventing the
 upgrade?
explanation: Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0 alongside Secure Boot and UEFI, and the compatibility check fails outright without it, which is the classic blocker on otherwise capable Windows 10 hardware. B (Slow HDD spindle speed), C (Low refresh rate) and D (High RAM latency) are performance characteristics that appear nowhere in Microsoft's minimum requirements, so they may make the machine feel sluggish but will not stop the upgrade.

question:
A user is unable to upload files to the corporate servers from their mobile phone when outside the office, but uploading files works without issue
 when they are in the office. The user briefly saw an error notification but dismissed the error before reading it. Which of the following should a
 technician do to determine the root cause?
explanation: Uploads succeed on office Wi-Fi but fail on cellular, which points at the mobile plan rather than the phone or the server; a carrier or on-device data cap throttles or blocks transfers and produces exactly that brief error notification. B (Enable airplane mode) kills every radio and makes things worse, C (Verify the last device reboot) reveals nothing about connectivity, and D (Bluetooth) is not the transport used to reach corporate servers.

question:
A desktop technician is mapping a remote windows share \\WinNAS\shared as a local disk z:. Which of the following commands should the
 technician run?
explanation: net use maps a drive letter to a UNC path, so net use Z: \\WinNAS\shared attaches the share as local disk Z:, with /persistent:yes to keep it across reboots. A (nslookup) only queries DNS records, C (chkdsk /R) scans a disk for bad sectors and attempts recovery, and D (sfc /offwindir) aims System File Checker at an offline Windows installation. None of those three create a drive mapping.

question:
A technician needs to change hibernation settings on a Windows computer by applying a batch file. Domain policies are unavailable. Which of the
 following is the best way to achieve this goal?

options.A: Update Power Options in the Control Panel.
options.C: Run gpupdate from a command prompt.
options.D: Use the powercfg command in PowerShell.

explanation: powercfg is the command-line power configuration tool, so a line such as powercfg /hibernate off drops straight into a batch file and runs without any policy infrastructure. A (Power Options in Control Panel) is a manual GUI change that cannot be scripted, B (firmware update) does not control Windows power states, and C (gpupdate) merely reapplies existing Group Policy, which the scenario says is unavailable.

question:
A client reports that their browser’s home page changed. Every time they run an internet search, the results returned are from unfamiliar websites.
 Which of the following actions should a technician take first to resolve the issue? (Choose two.)

options.C: Check the system date and time.

explanation: A changed home page plus redirected search results is the signature of a browser hijacker riding in as an add-on, so D (Uninstall malicious extensions) removes the component doing the redirecting and E (Reset the browser startup page) undoes the setting it altered. Do both, or the extension simply re-applies the page. A (Clear the browsing history) deletes records rather than the hijacker, and B (Run OS updates) and F (Restart the machine) leave the malicious add-on installed.

question:
A Windows user is having trouble accessing a fileshare. The technician would like to confirm the username that the machine is currently logged in
 to. Which of the following should the technician use?
explanation: whoami prints the domain and username of the account running the current session, which is exactly the confirmation needed before troubleshooting share permissions. A (net user) lists or edits account properties but does not report who is signed in right now, B (tracert) traces the network path to a remote host, and D (hostname) returns the computer's name instead of the user's.

question:
A technician follows the proper procedure for malware removal on an infected computer. However, the technician is unable to remove all the
 malware and decides to reload the OS. Which of the following should the technician select?
explanation: A clean install wipes the drive and lays down a fresh OS, the only option that guarantees leftover malware and infected system files are gone. B (System restore) rolls back to a snapshot that may already be infected, and restore points are normally disabled during malware removal anyway. C (OS repair) preserves the existing installation and its files, and A (Version upgrade) just layers a newer release on top of a compromised system.

question:
A technician is 3-D printing high strength, carbon fiber-based filament parts for a customer order. Which of the following is the most important for
 the technician to use?
explanation: Carbon-fiber composite filament sheds fine particulates and ultrafine plastic fumes as it is extruded, so respiratory protection with a properly rated filter mask, backed by good ventilation, is the priority. A (Steel-toed boots) guards against dropped heavy objects, while C (ESD mat) and D (Antistatic bags) protect electronic components from static discharge, which is not the hazard when printing filament parts.

question: Which of the following concepts should a technician consider when discussing confidential work projects with individuals outside the company?
explanation: A non-disclosure agreement is the contract that legally binds an outside party to keep project details confidential, so it must be signed before those discussions happen. A (EULA) governs how licensed software may be used, B (EOL) marks the end of a product's supported life, and C (SLA) sets uptime and response targets for a service. None of those three restrict what information can be shared.

question:
A technician is reviewing an organization's current incident management policy. The organization uses a third-party vendor to protect the
 organization's assets with multiple tools. Which of the following service types is the organization using?
explanation: Managed detection and response means an outside provider supplies both the tooling and the analysts who monitor, investigate and respond on the organization's behalf, which matches a third-party vendor protecting assets with multiple tools. B (EDR) is endpoint-only software the company would operate itself, D (XDR) correlates telemetry across endpoints, network and cloud but is still a product rather than a managed service, and A (PaaS) is a cloud development platform.

question: Which of the following commands can a technician use to view the contents of a single file on a Linux terminal?
explanation: cat concatenates a file to standard output, making it the fastest way to display the contents of a single file at the terminal. A (chmod) changes permission bits, C (ls) lists directory entries without revealing what is inside any file, and D (sudo) only runs another command with elevated privileges rather than displaying anything itself.

question:
A Chief Executive Officer wants to meet with remote employees in a way that will allow for collaboration and training. Which of the following
 software technologies is the best for this situation?
explanation: Videoconferencing carries two-way audio and video among many participants, which is what makes live collaboration and training sessions work. B (Screen sharing) pushes one desktop's view and is normally just a feature inside a conferencing tool, while C (RDP) and D (VDI) give an individual remote control of a desktop or virtual machine, useful for working remotely but not for hosting a group meeting.

question: Which of the following filesystems supports read and write operations for Windows, macOS, and Linux?
explanation: exFAT was designed as a cross-platform successor to FAT32 and has native read/write support on Windows, macOS and Linux, without FAT32's 4GB file size limit. C (NTFS) is read-only on macOS without third-party drivers, B (ReFS) is Windows-only, D (APFS) is Apple's own filesystem, and E (ext4) needs extra software before Windows or macOS can touch it.

question:
A technician recently installed a program that uses several anti-piracy technologies. When the program is launched, it briefly opens and then
 closes. Which of the following is most likely the reason?
explanation: Many anti-piracy schemes depend on a hardware dongle, so with the USB key absent the licence check fails the instant the program starts and it closes itself. A (32-bit program on a 64-bit computer) runs happily under WoW64, B (CPU incompatibility) normally prevents launch with a specific error message, and C (Outdated video card drivers) causes graphical glitches or crashes during use rather than an immediate silent exit.

question:
A computer frequently crashes after an OS patch. Which of the following actions should a technician take to prevent further crashes and look into
 the issue?
explanation: Rolling back the update removes the specific patch that introduced the instability, keeps the machine usable while the cause is investigated, and the update can then be paused so it does not reinstall. A (System Restore) reverts far more than the patch and may not target it cleanly, C (Apply the optional patches) piles more change onto an unstable system, and D (Change the startup sequence) alters boot order, which has nothing to do with patching.

question:
After a user installs a mobile application from an advertisement, the phone’s battery dies a few hours later, and it is hot to touch, even when not in
 use. Which of the following should a technician do first?

options.C: Run a mobile malware scan on the phone.
options.D: Ensure appropriate MDM policies are applied.

explanation: Rapid battery drain and a hot device while idle, starting right after an app installed from an advert, are classic signs of malicious code running in the background, so a mobile anti-malware scan confirms it first. A (Check for unauthorized device administrators) is a sensible follow-up but narrower, B (Contact the software developer) assumes the app is legitimate, and D (MDM policies) is a preventive control that does nothing for an already infected phone.

question:
After new device software for a webcam is installed, a Windows PC is experiencing BSOD. The BSOD occurs during a videoconference call. Which
 of the following should the technician do next?

options.A: Update the anti-malware signatures and scan the system.
options.B: File a warranty claim with the manufacturer.
options.C: Start in safe mode and roll back the device driver.
options.D: Reconnect the webcam to the computer.

explanation: The stop errors began immediately after new webcam software was installed, so the new driver is the prime suspect; safe mode loads a minimal driver set, keeping the system stable long enough to roll the driver back in Device Manager. A (anti-malware scan) chases an unrelated cause, B (warranty claim) is premature for a software fault, and D (Reconnect the webcam) does nothing about the faulty driver still loading at boot.

question:
A technician is setting up a computer for a new user. A requirement is that the user’s documents are stored on a network location and not locally
 on the computer. Which of the following should the technician configure?
explanation: Folder redirection points known folders such as Documents at a network share, so everything the user saves lands on the server rather than the local disk, transparently and without retraining the user. A (File attributes) sets flags like read-only or hidden, B (User Account Control) prompts for elevation, and C (Security groups) governs who may access a resource. None of them change where files are stored.

question:
An end user wants to have a sales printer added to their computer. The printer is on the domain. Which of the following is the best method for the
 technician to add the printer?

options.A: Go to the print server and select the printer name.
options.B: Connect the laptop to the printer via USB.
options.C: Connect to the printer via Bluetooth.
options.D: Go to Local User and Groups to add the printer.

explanation: A domain printer is published through the print server, so browsing to the server and selecting the shared printer installs the correct driver and queue while keeping the printer centrally managed and updated. B (USB) and C (Bluetooth) create a local single-user connection that bypasses the shared queue and its drivers entirely, and D (Local Users and Groups) manages accounts, not printers.

question: Which of the following authentication methods is the best way to prevent users from frequently entering their credentials?
explanation: Single sign-on authenticates the user once and then issues a token that other trusted applications accept, so credentials are not retyped at every resource. C (Multifactor authentication) and D (One-time password) deliberately add steps to each login rather than removing them, and A (Access control list) is an authorization mechanism defining who may access an object, not an authentication method at all.

question:
A secretary receives an email from the company's chief executive officer with a request to pay a vendor immediately. After the payment is made,
 the chief executive officer tells the secretary that they never sent that email. Which of the following social engineering tactics best describes this
 type of attack?
explanation: B (Impersonation) fits, because the attacker is posing as the CEO to make a trusted request the secretary will act on — the tactic commonly called CEO fraud or business email compromise. C (Whaling) means the executive is the intended victim, not the mask being worn. D (Spear phishing) describes a targeted email built on researched details, and A (Evil twin) is a rogue wireless access point, not an email tactic. Some sources do key an item like this as whaling because an executive is involved at all, so expect to see it argued both ways.

question:
Performance on a user's smartphone is degrading. Applications take a long time to start, and switching between windows also takes a long time.
 Which of the following diagnostic steps should a mobile technician take first?

options.A: Restore the phone to factory settings.

explanation: Phones accumulate stuck background processes and leaked memory, and a restart clears RAM and restarts services, making it the quickest and least destructive first step for general sluggishness. A (Restore to factory settings) destroys data and is a last resort, D (Uninstall unneeded applications) is worth doing later once a culprit is identified, and C (Check the battery state) better explains sudden shutdowns or throttling than slow app switching.

question: A user is unable to use the latest version of an application on a legacy, personal tablet. Which of the following is most likely the reason?

options.D: The tablet is infected with malware.

explanation: Once a tablet's OS reaches end of life it stops receiving version updates, and current app builds target a newer minimum OS version, so the store refuses to install or run the latest release. B (Storage space) produces an explicit install error that is easily cleared, C (MDM) does not apply to a personal device, and D (malware) causes instability and pop-ups rather than one app cleanly refusing to run.

question: Which of the following is used to store passwords in macOS?
explanation: Keychain is the macOS credential store that holds passwords, certificates and secure notes, unlocked by the account password and managed through Keychain Access. A (FileVault) provides full-disk encryption, C (Accessibility) covers assistive settings such as VoiceOver and zoom, and D (Mission Control) arranges windows, spaces and virtual desktops.

question:
A user logs in to a computer each morning and tries to print a daily report, but it will not print. The user calls the help desk, they change a setting,
 and the user is able to print that day but the same issue happens again the next day. Because the issue occurs every day, the issue gets escalated.
 Which of the following does the technician need to do so the user does not have to report the issue every day? (Choose two.)

options.A: Set the print spooler to have no dependencies.
options.B: Set the print spooler recovery to take no action.
options.C: Start the printer extensions and notifications service.
options.E: Set the print spooler to Automatic.
options.F: Set the print spooler log-on to the user’s account.

explanation: The print spooler is stopping between sessions and the help desk is simply starting it again each morning, so D (Start the print spooler service) restores printing now and E (Set the print spooler to Automatic) makes it start itself at every boot, which permanently ends the daily call. B (recovery set to take no action) would stop it restarting after a failure, and F (log-on as the user's account) breaks a service that must run as Local System.

question:
A user’s computer is able to access resources on the corporate network but is unable to access internet web pages with a browser. Which of the
 following is most likely the reason?
explanation: Internal resources still resolve and load, so the network stack is healthy; corporate internet access that is forced through a proxy fails when the browser is not pointed at that proxy or its script. A (IP address conflict) and C (Incorrect subnet mask) would disrupt local traffic as well, and D (Disconnected Ethernet cable) would cut off the corporate network too, not just web browsing.

question:
A technician needs to download and install a new web browser on a desktop computer. Which of the following should the technician use to verify
 the installer is an authentic version?
explanation: Vendors publish a checksum for their installers, so hashing the downloaded file and comparing the value proves the bytes match what the publisher released and catches tampering or a corrupt download. A (Date), C (Size) and D (Name) are metadata an attacker can trivially match while still altering the file's contents, so none of them establish authenticity.

question:
A Microsoft OS laptop user requests an alternative log-in authentication method because they have forgotten their password multiple times.
 Which of the following should a technician enable to satisfy this request?
explanation: Windows Hello provides alternative sign-in methods such as facial recognition, fingerprint or a device-bound PIN, letting a user who keeps forgetting the password authenticate without typing it. A (Single sign-on) reuses the same credentials across services, C (BitLocker) encrypts the drive, and D (User Account Control) prompts before elevated actions. None of them replaces the login method itself.

question:
A Windows 11 Home device is receiving constant pop-ups about an urgent need to update antivirus software in order to remove a detected threat.
 The user has been clicking the "X" button in the window frame, but it always reappears. The pop-up includes an "OK" button to install the update
 and remove the threat. Which of the following should the user do next?

options.A: Click the "OK" button to install the update.
options.D: Verify the current status and settings of protection measures.

explanation: The pop-up is classic scareware, so the safe move is to ignore its buttons entirely and verify the machine's real protection status, confirming Windows Security is enabled and definitions are current before running a scan. A (Click OK) installs the rogue software the scam is selling, B (Reinstall Windows) is drastic with nothing yet confirmed, and C (System File Checker) repairs corrupt Windows files, which a browser pop-up does not indicate.

question:
A customer reports that a computer is displaying pop-ups and making unexpected sounds. Which of the following should a technician do before
 remediating this issue?
explanation: Quarantine comes immediately after identifying and verifying symptoms in the malware removal process, so disconnecting the machine from the network stops the infection spreading or communicating out while it is worked on. A (Back up the customer's data) risks copying infected files off the system, B (Update the OS) belongs after remediation, and C (Reimage the workstation) is a last resort that destroys data and evidence.

question:
A company wants to use its directory database to authenticate users to its wireless network. Which of the following should the company use to
 accomplish this task?
explanation: RADIUS is the AAA server that sits between the wireless infrastructure and the directory: the access point passes 802.1X credentials to it, and it validates them against the existing user database. D (LDAP) is the protocol used to query that directory but cannot itself perform network access authentication, B (WPA3) is the encryption standard the WLAN runs, and A (MFA) adds a second factor rather than linking Wi-Fi to the directory.

question:
A user takes an iOS-based smartphone that is performing slowly to a repair shop. A shop technician finds the following information:
 Battery charge: 25%
 Battery health: 90%
 Hotspot: On -
 Mobile reception: |||
 Roaming: Off -
 Used space: 63.76GB/64GB -
 Which of the following is the cause of the issue?

options.A: The device is running out of free space
options.C: The phone is not sufficiently charged.
options.D: The hotspot is degrading the performance.

explanation: With 63.76GB of 64GB consumed, the phone has essentially no room for caching, temporary files or app data, and iOS slows badly once free space runs out. B (Battery health) at 90% is perfectly healthy, C (25% charge) does not throttle the device unless low power mode is on, and D (Hotspot) consumes bandwidth and battery rather than slowing the interface.

question: Which of the following controls access to certain services to ensure that administrators are not automatically given elevated permissions?
explanation: Privileged access management strips standing administrative rights and grants elevation only on request, for a limited window and to a defined service, so an admin account is not automatically powerful. B (MFA) strengthens how identity is proven, C (DLP) prevents sensitive data leaving the organization, and D (SSO) reduces repeated logins. None of those three limit what an administrator's account can reach.

question: Which of the following filesystems is a successor to NTFS?
explanation: ReFS, the Resilient File System, is Microsoft's next-generation filesystem intended to succeed NTFS, adding integrity streams, automatic error correction and support for far larger volumes and files in Storage Spaces. B (XFS) is a Linux filesystem, C (APFS) is Apple's replacement for HFS+, and D (exFAT) is a lightweight FAT successor aimed at removable media rather than enterprise storage.

question:
A technician needs to configure settings for password complexity and failed log-in attempts before a user is locked out. These settings cannot be
 changed by standard users. Which of the following MMC snap-ins should the technician use?
explanation: Password complexity, minimum length and account lockout thresholds live under Account Policies in Security Settings, edited through the Local Group Policy Editor (gpedit.msc), and they apply machine-wide beyond a standard user's reach. B (lusrmgr) manages individual accounts and group membership but exposes no policy settings, A (taskschd) schedules jobs, and C (perfmon) collects performance counters.

question:
A customer is upgrading their workstation from Windows 10 to Windows 11. They perform a clean installation from a USB drive. After the system
 restarts, the installer loads again. Which of the following should the user do to complete the installation?
explanation: The firmware is still booting from the installation media, so setup launches all over again; removing the USB drive (or fixing the boot order) lets the system boot the freshly installed OS and finish out-of-box setup. B (Turn off TPM) removes a Windows 11 requirement, C (Change MBR to UEFI) addresses a partition-scheme error that would have blocked setup earlier, and A (chkdsk) does not influence boot order.

question:
A user called the help desk to report an issue with the internet connection speed on a laptop. The technician thinks that background services may
 be using extra bandwidth. Which of the following tools should the technician use to investigate connections on the laptop?
explanation: netstat lists active TCP and UDP connections plus listening ports, and with -b or -o it ties each connection to the owning process, exposing which background service is consuming bandwidth. A (nslookup) only resolves DNS names, B (net use) manages drive mappings, and D (net user) queries account information rather than network sessions.

question:
A user is unable to log in to the network. The network uses 802.1X with EAP-TLS to authenticate on the wired network. The user has been on an
 extended leave and has not logged in to the computer in several months. Which of the following is causing the login issue?
explanation: EAP-TLS authenticates with client certificates that carry a fixed validity period, so after months away the machine or user certificate has expired without being renewed and the 802.1X exchange fails, leaving the switch port unauthorized. B (OS update failure), C (Service not started) and E (Profile rebuild needed) have no particular link to elapsed time, and D (Application crash) does not affect network-level authentication.

question: Which of the following authentication methods is token-based?
explanation: A (Kerberos) is the token-based method: after authenticating, the client receives a ticket-granting ticket and then per-service tickets, so the token rather than the password is presented to each resource. D (TKIP) is not an authentication method at all — it is the encryption protocol WPA wrapped around RC4. B (TACACS+) is an AAA protocol that carries credentials to a central server, and C (Passwords) are a knowledge factor with no token involved.

question: Which of the following is the most secure method of preventing someone from accessing a cell phone?
explanation: A passphrase is the longest and most varied secret of the four, drawing many characters from a large character set, so brute-forcing it takes vastly more attempts. A (PIN) is normally only four to six digits, and B (Swipe) and D (Pattern) offer a small pool of practical combinations while leaving smudge trails on the screen that make them easy to reproduce.

question: When a user is in the office, web pages are loading slowly on the user's phone. Which of the following best explains this issue?
explanation: Slowness confined to one location points at the network serving that location, where congestion, weak signal or an overloaded access point degrades throughput for the phone while the device itself is fine. A (Exceeded the data usage limit) would follow the user everywhere rather than stopping at the office door, D (Low storage space) slows the whole device, and B (Sluggish response time) simply restates the symptom instead of explaining it.

question:
A user calls the help desk to report potential malware on a computer. The anomalous activity began after the user clicked a link to a free gift card
 in a recent email. The technician asks the user to describe any unusual activity, such as slow performance, excessive pop-ups, and browser
 redirections.
 Which of the following should the technician do next?

options.A: Advise the user to run a complete system scan using the OS anti-malware application.
options.B: Guide the user to reboot the machine into safe mode and verify whether the anomalous activities are still present.
options.C: Have the user check for recently installed applications and outline those installed since the link in the email was clicked.
options.D: Instruct the user to disconnect the Ethernet connection to the corporate network.

explanation: Symptoms have already been gathered, so the next step in the malware removal process is quarantine: pulling the Ethernet connection isolates the machine so nothing spreads laterally or exfiltrates data. A (Run a complete system scan) and B (Reboot into safe mode) are remediation and investigation steps that belong after isolation, and C (Check recently installed applications) leaves the compromised machine sitting on the corporate network.

question:
A technician is installing a new business application on a user's desktop computer. The machine is running Windows 10 Enterprise 32-bit
 operating system. Which of the following files should the technician execute in order to complete the installation?
explanation: x86 is the standard label for a 32-bit build, so Installer_x86.exe is the one that will actually run on 32-bit Windows 10 Enterprise. A (Installer_x64.exe) is a 64-bit binary that a 32-bit OS cannot execute, E (.dmg) is a macOS disk image, B (Installer_Files.zip) is only an archive with nothing to execute until extracted, and C (Installer_32.msi) is a Windows Installer package rather than the vendor's installer executable.

question:
A user created a file on a shared drive and wants to prevent its data from being accidentally deleted by others. Which of the following applications
 should the technician use to assist the user with hiding the file?
explanation: The Hidden attribute is set from the file's Properties dialog in File Explorer, which keeps the file out of ordinary folder views so it is far less likely to be deleted by accident. A (Device Manager) handles hardware and drivers, B (Indexing Options) tunes search behaviour, and D (Administrative Tools) is a folder of management consoles with no per-file attribute control.

question:
A technician is performing an in-place upgrade on a user's laptop. Which of the following is the most effective method of upgrading the
 workstation to the latest OS?

options.A: Utilize the latest version of the .iso file.
options.B: Back up data and perform a fresh installation.
options.C: Enter the BIOS and enable USB access.

explanation: An in-place upgrade preserves applications, settings and data, and the built-in System Update utility pulls the correct build, runs the compatibility checks and migrates everything automatically. B (Back up data and perform a fresh installation) is a clean install, the opposite of in place, C (enable USB access in BIOS) only concerns booting external media, and A (latest .iso) is a manual route that reaches the same upgrade path with more steps and more risk.

question: Which of the following is used to identify potential issues with a proposed change prior to implementation?
explanation: Sandbox testing runs the proposed change in an isolated environment that mirrors production, so failures, conflicts and unwanted side effects surface before any user is affected. A (Request form) documents and justifies the change, B (Rollback plan) is the fallback used after a change goes wrong, and C (End-user acceptance) confirms the outcome is workable only once the change has already been applied.

question:
Each time a user tries to go to the selected web search provider, a different website opens. Which of the following should the technician check
 first?
explanation: Searches landing on unintended sites usually means name resolution is being redirected, so check the adapter's configured DNS servers, and the hosts file, for entries the user did not set. A (System time) breaks certificate validation rather than sending traffic elsewhere, B (IP address) problems would stop connectivity altogether, and D (Windows updates) has no bearing on where a hostname resolves.

question:
A user receives a notification indicating the antivirus protection on a company laptop is out of date. A technician is able to ping the user’s laptop.
 The technician checks the antivirus parent servers and sees the latest signatures have been installed. The technician then checks the user's
 laptop and finds the antivirus engine and definitions are current. Which of the following has most likely occurred?
explanation: C (Adware) is the culprit: the parent servers show current signatures and the laptop is reachable, so the antivirus really is up to date and the out-of-date warning is a fake pop-up planted to push the user toward a bogus product. D (Missing system files) would produce application or boot errors, not a targeted antivirus notice. A (Ransomware) announces itself with encrypted files and a demand, and B (Failed OS updates) would surface in Windows Update rather than as an antivirus alert.

question: Which of the following would an administrator most likely use to automate a repetitive task via a Linux command line?
explanation: A shell script collects Linux commands into an executable file the shell runs in order, which is the native way to automate repetitive command-line work and hand it to cron for scheduling. D (Batch file) and C (Visual Basic utilities) are Windows scripting formats, and A (JavaScript file) requires a runtime such as Node and is not the standard tool for Linux system administration.

question: Which of the following is used to determine how many active users are currently logged in to the Remote Desktop Services?
explanation: Task Manager's Users tab lists every session on the machine, including active and disconnected Remote Desktop sessions and the resources each one is consuming. A (Local Users and Groups) shows which accounts exist rather than who is connected, B (System Information) reports hardware and OS configuration, and C (Group Policy Editor) sets policy instead of reporting live session state.

question: Which of the following grants a user the minimum level of permissions necessary to perform duties?
explanation: Least privilege grants each account only the rights its role genuinely requires and nothing more, limiting the damage when an account is misused or compromised. B (Zero Trust) is the wider architecture of never trusting a request implicitly and verifying every one, while C (SSO) and D (MFA) concern how a user proves identity rather than what that identity is permitted to do.

question:
A technician is creating an MDM policy using hardening techniques that are unique to each user. Which of the following techniques is the
 technician using?
explanation: A fingerprint is biometric, derived from the individual's own physical characteristics, so it is inherently unique to each user and cannot be shared, guessed or handed over. A (A drawn pattern), C (A password) and D (A PIV card) are things a user knows or holds, all of which can be copied, lent to a colleague or reused, so none of them is unique to the person.

question: Which of the following operating systems is used to join a domain?
explanation: Domain join is a business feature reserved for the Pro, Enterprise and Education editions, so Windows 11 Pro is the one here that can be added to an Active Directory domain. A (Windows 10 Home) and B (Windows 11 Home) are limited to workgroups or a Microsoft account, and D (Windows 11 SE) is a locked-down education edition managed through Intune rather than a domain.

question:
When a user navigates to comptiaa.org, pop-up messages indicate that the computer is infected with adware. A technician scans the computer
 for malware and does not find an infection. Which of the following should the technician do before returning the computer to the user?

options.A: Clear the browser's cached data and recent history.
options.B: Sign in to the company's cloud workspace application.
options.D: Enable private mode for using the internet.

explanation: No infection is present, so the alerts came from the site itself, and clearing the browser's cache, cookies and history removes the stored scripts and entries that keep bringing them back. B (Sign in to the cloud workspace) is unrelated, D (Enable private mode) does nothing about data already saved in the profile, and C (Install corporate DNS security software) is a broader preventive measure rather than the cleanup this machine needs before handover.

question: A technician must add an external web address as a trusted site. Which of the following settings should the technician configure?
explanation: Trusted sites are managed in Internet Options, on the Security tab, where the URL is added to the Trusted Sites zone and inherits that zone's relaxed restrictions. A (System) covers device name and performance settings, B (Network and Sharing Center) handles adapters and network profiles, and D (Administrative Tools) is a collection of management consoles with no browser zone configuration.
